title: Four days.
paragraphs:
Not sick.
Not struggling.
Not “almost gone.”

And if you’re honest…
there’s something in your life that feels exactly like that.

But what if the delay…
was never denial?

What if God waited…
on purpose?

Some of us don’t need healing anymore.
We need resurrection.
Because this isn’t just about pain.

The kind you don’t post.
The kind you hide behind church smiles.
The kind that whispers at night:

“You’ve gone too far.”
“You’ve done too much.”
“You can’t come back from this.”

No movement.
No breath.
No hope.
In fact, when Jesus finally arrives, Martha says it straight:
“Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.” (John 11:39)
But here’s the tension you didn’t notice.
“So, when He heard that Lazarus was ill, He stayed two days longer…” (John 11:6)
Why would God allow it to get worse?
Some scholars interpret that in Jewish belief, the soul was thought to linger near the body for three days—but by the fourth day, death was final and irreversible.
He showed up when no one could explain it away.

Not coincidence.
Not recovery.
Not timing.
And this is where it gets uncomfortable.

“Lord, fix this now.”
“Lord, remove this today.”
“Lord, don’t let it get worse.”
God lets it reach four days.

Crowds watching.
Grief hanging heavy in the air.
The One who knew He would raise Lazarus…
Still felt the pain of death.
This is not a distant Savior.
This is God who steps into your mess, your shame, your broken places—and feels it with you.
He doesn’t rush past your pain.
And this is where many of us stop.
But we don’t want to roll the stone away.
But we hide the very thing He wants to bring back to life.
“Did I not tell you that if you believed you would see the glory of God?” (John 11:40)
The shout that split death open:
And a man who was four days dead…

Still wrapped.
Still marked by death.
He exposed the lie that anything is too far gone.

Not your past.
Not your addiction.
Not your hidden sin.
Not your shame.
But here’s the truth we can’t soften:
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
This is where the Gospel breaks in.

Not self-help.
Not religion.
Not behavior management.
The same Jesus who stood at Lazarus’ tomb…
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)

Your shame.
Your guilt.
Your سزا (punishment).
“I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me, though he die, yet shall he live.” (John 11:25)
He offers that life to you.

Turning from sin.
Turning to Him.
What have you sealed in the tomb?
What are you hoping no one sees?
What have you already declared “too far gone”?
Because Jesus is standing there right now.
Because grace cannot resurrect what pride keeps buried.
And when He calls your name—

“Jesus, I’m done hiding.
I’m done pretending.
I give You everything—even the parts that stink.
Forgive me.
Change me.
Call me out of this tomb.”
four days is not too late.
From shame to resurrection—because Jesus still calls the dead to life.
